concept.title: PDF with DesignSystemPDF
concept.shortdesc: DesignSystemPDF is the plugin's companion: it renders the print document as a page-numbered, tagged PDF, with Java as the only requirement. Install it beside the toolkit and the build finds it, makes the PDF and links it from the site.

conbody.p: DesignSystemPDFPDFDesignSystemPDFThe plugin makes websites and stays small: it holds no PDF engine and no fonts. DesignSystemPDF is a second product from the same project that does that one job. It is released on its own, with its own version numbers; it is not a DITA-OT plugin and is never installed into the toolkit. The two meet through one file, the print document, so each can be upgraded without the other.

section.title: What it adds
section.p: From the print document the build already writes (), unchanged:

ul.li: page numbers in the contents list, in the index and on every cross-reference;
footnotes at the foot of the page that calls them, with the author's own marker;
running heads — the publication's title and the chapter's — on every page after the cover;
an outline of bookmarks from the headings, and the title and author from the cover in the PDF's own properties;
a tagged PDF that meets PDF/UA-1, the accessibility standard for PDF, with every font embedded;
repeated table headers, and landscape pages for a table or figure marked outputclass="landscape";
the same bytes from the same input, and no network request: it suits a build server as well as a desk.

section.title: Installing it
section.p: DesignSystemPDFinstallingYou need Java 17 or later, which the toolkit needs too, so a machine that builds the site already has it.

ol.li: Download designsystempdf-version.zip from the releases page of . DesignSystemPDF's releases are the ones whose tags begin pdf-v; the plugin's begin v.

Check the download against the checksum published beside it: sha256sum -c designsystempdf-version.zip.sha256 On Windows, Get-FileHash in PowerShell gives the checksum to compare with the one in that file.
Unzip it anywhere outside the toolkit, and put its bin folder on the PATH.
Confirm it runs: designsystempdf --version It prints its version and the print contracts it understands.

section.p: Nothing is installed into the toolkit and nothing is downloaded when it runs. To upgrade, unzip the newer release in place of the old one.

section.title: Using it with the plugin
section.p: govuk.pdfWith DesignSystemPDF on the PATH, ask the build for the print document and nothing more:

The build finds DesignSystemPDF as it finds Pagefind for search, and says so in its log. It writes the site, then the print document, then runs DesignSystemPDF on it. The result is in the output folder beside print.html:

ul.li: publication.pdf, named after the map, or after govuk.pdf.name if you set it;
a link to it on the home page and in every footer, beside the print version, with its size: Whole publication (PDF, 1.2 MB).

section.p: The paper size and orientation come from govuk.pdf.paper and govuk.pdf.orientation, the same parameters that set them for printing from a browser, so the PDF and a browser's print agree. The depth of the bookmarks follows govuk.print.toc.depth, up to 6, and fonts of your own come from the folder named in govuk.pdf.fonts.
govuk.pdf decides whether the PDF is made:

strow.stentry: auto (default)
Make the PDF when DesignSystemPDF is found and govuk.print=yes; otherwise build the site without one, and say why in the log.
Stop the build at the start if DesignSystemPDF is not found or govuk.print is not yes. Use it on a build server, where a missing PDF should not go unnoticed.
Make no PDF, even with DesignSystemPDF installed.

section.p: If DesignSystemPDF is not on the PATH, give the path to its launcher in govuk.pdf.cmd: bin/designsystempdf, or bin\designsystempdf.bat on Windows. If it cannot be run, or fails, the build reports GOVK008W with DesignSystemPDF's own messages and finishes: the site is complete, and no page links a PDF that is not there.

section.title: Options
section.p: govuk.pdf.commandThe build passes DesignSystemPDF the paper, the bookmark depth and the fonts. For any other option, name the command yourself in govuk.pdf.command, which is then run in place of the one the build finds. Options go before the two file names the plugin adds; quote the whole parameter so the spaces survive:

strow.stentry: standard (the default: 20 mm top, 18 mm sides, 22 mm bottom), narrow, wide, or one to four CSS lengths.
single (the default), or double for mirrored margins with a wider inner margin for binding.
A folder of TrueType fonts of your own, used where the stylesheets name their families. Through the plugin, set govuk.pdf.fonts instead.
Depth of the bookmarks, 1 to 6; 3 by default. The depth of the printed contents list is the plugin's govuk.print.toc.depth.
The date written into the PDF, such as 2026-10-01. Without it no date is written, so the same input gives the same file.
Write an untagged PDF. The default is tagged PDF/UA-1; keep it for anything you publish.
--paper, --orientation
Override the paper for the PDF alone. Prefer the plugin's govuk.pdf.paper and govuk.pdf.orientation, which set it for browsers as well.
Report progress and the engine's own diagnostics.

section.p: It also runs by hand on a print document already built, which is the quickest way to try an option:
section.codeblock: cd out designsystempdf --sides double print.html publication.pdf
section.p: A PDF made by hand is not linked from the site; the link is added by the build that makes the PDF.

section.title: Fonts
section.p: fontsin PDFA tagged PDF must embed every font it uses, and a build should give the same result on every machine, so DesignSystemPDF never uses the fonts installed on the computer. It carries Noto Sans and Noto Sans Mono, which are free to redistribute, and uses them wherever the stylesheets ask for a font it has not been given.

To use others, put their TrueType (.ttf) files in a folder and name it in govuk.pdf.fonts (or pass --fonts when running DesignSystemPDF yourself). An organisation entitled to GDS Transport or Frutiger supplies its own licensed files this way; neither is ever shipped (). A supplied font is also used for any character the other fonts cannot draw, so a publication with passages in a script the bundled fonts lack needs only a font that has it.

section.title: When something is wrong
section.p: DesignSystemPDF's messages have codes beginning DSPDF, and the build log shows them as they are: as warnings under the line the PDF command reported when the PDF is made, and with GOVK008W when it is not. The ones a publisher is most likely to meet:

strow.stentry: The print document was written to a contract this release does not understand, and no PDF is written. Upgrade DesignSystemPDF, or the plugin, whichever is the older.

Some characters have no glyph in the fonts and print as a replacement mark. Supply a font that covers them with govuk.pdf.fonts; it is used for those characters without your stylesheet having to name it.
The publication has text in a right-to-left script, which will not read correctly in the PDF whatever fonts are supplied. See the known defect below.

The contents could not be laid out with dots between the titles and the page numbers, so it has the page numbers alone; the rest of the PDF is as usual. Report it, with the print document. (DesignSystemPDF 0.1.0 wrote no PDF at all here, with DSPDF007E, for some publications of a thousand pages or more.)
An image or stylesheet on another website was not fetched; nothing is requested over the network. Keep the file with the publication.
An image, diagram or formula has no alternative text, so the PDF does not meet PDF/UA. Add the text in the DITA source.

section.p: Warnings never stop the PDF being written. The full list, the exit codes and the limits — one paper size per publication, PDF/A is not produced — are in the README.md inside the download.

section.title: Known defect: right-to-left scripts
section.p: right-to-left textin PDFDesignSystemPDFknown defectsDesignSystemPDF 0.1 does not render text in a right-to-left script, such as Arabic or Hebrew. The website and the print document are right — the page is marked with its language and direction and the text runs from the right — but in the PDF every such character prints as a replacement mark and the topic is set from the left. The build log says so with DSPDF010W, and lists the characters that have no glyph with DSPDF004W.
Supplying a font with govuk.pdf.fonts does not cure it. The letters then appear, but unjoined and running from the left, so the text is still unreadable; DSPDF010W is given all the same.

Until this is fixed, make the PDF of a right-to-left publication, or of one with right-to-left passages, from a browser: open print.html and use the browser's print or save-as-PDF command. Browsers shape and order the text correctly; the contents list and index then carry links instead of page numbers (). Build such a publication with govuk.pdf=no, so that the site does not link a PDF with unreadable passages.

section.title: Which versions work together
section.p: print contractThe print document carries a marker, the print contract, that changes only when the structure a formatter relies on changes. A release of DesignSystemPDF lists the contracts it understands, and refuses a document with another instead of rendering it wrongly.

strow.stentry: 1.0.1 and later 1.x

section.p: From plugin 1.1.0 the build finds DesignSystemPDF on the PATH for itself and links the PDF from the site. With 1.0.1, name it in govuk.pdf.command: the PDF is made, but nothing links it.
